alt: A kitchen-dining room with a stone trough sink built into lacquered burl cabinetry, shown in four distinct material schemes varying plaster wall colours, cabinet finishes, floor tones and textiles. Each scheme creates a different warm jewel-tone palette while maintaining the same architectural structure, deco furniture language, and mountain lake view through glazed panels at overcast dusk.
text:
one kitchen in four material stories
the rust, pink, olive, pale schemes — each catches light differently through lacquered burl, plaster, stone. depth grows from how materials age, not from colour alone. the trough and joinery stay fixed. the floors and walls rearrange.
#kitchendesign #stonetrough #lacqueredjoinery #materialstudy #jeweltonespalette

quality_notes: dropped — scheme 4: every surface is the same saturated colour (saturation 0.56, hues within 9°) — the whole room was painted one shade
note: Too simple, and the room fails basic object logic: two facing counters each with its own tap — a real kitchen has one sink — and the dining table is parked in the middle of the galley walkway. The composition is dead mirror symmetry around a one-point axis, which reads as a rendering, not a place. The ask stands: wide-angle rooms that are richly layered and detailed, with every fixture appearing once and furniture where it belongs.
